newsitem.title: USA: Defense rests in Oklahoma City bombing trial.
newsitem.headline: Defense rests in Oklahoma City bombing trial.

text.p: The defense rested its case Wednesday in the trial of accused Oklahoma City bomber Timothy McVeigh.
The attorneys concluded after four days and 25 witnesses. The prosecution now has an opportunity to present rebuttal witnesses.
The first rebuttal witness to appear was Marife Nichols, the wife of McVeigh's alleged co-conspirator Terry Nichols who will be tried separately.

She testified earlier in the trial that on Easter Sunday 1995, three days before the bombing, her husband was called away suddenly in mid-afternoon in Junction City, Kansas, and did not return until the following morning.
Prosecutors claim McVeigh called Nichols that afternoon and the two then drove to Oklahoma City to drop off the getaway car allegedly used in the blast.

With the trial moving much more quickly than expected, the jury could begin deliberating as early as Friday. If convicted of the federal murder and conspiracy charges, the 29-year-old McVeigh faces the death penalty.
